summary: autotel-terminal 33.0.0: static patterns match keyword co-occurrence in bundled CLI without traced installer-harm path
details: Package ships bundled CLI files dist/cli.cjs and dist/cli.js. Static keyword co-occurrence patterns match in these bundles: Buffer.from(..., 'base64').toString(...) decoding at lines 119-120 and 204-210, and 'ping' (line 467) alongside multiple 'POST' occurrences (lines 318-321, 413-414). Base64 decoding and POST calls are common primitives in legitimate CLI/SDK code and are not, on their own, evidence of exfiltration; no specific installer-owned secret is shown being read, and no specific attacker-controlled destination is identified in the matched evidence. Without traced code reachability at install/import time or a named exfil destination, the observed patterns are consistent with either a legitimate terminal/CLI tool or a malicious one.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
